doc.verdict: Fixed off-by-one slice in paginate() when page is 1.

parts.heading: Cause
parts.prose: `start` used `page * size` instead of `(page - 1) * size`, skipping page 1.

parts.heading: Change
parts.before:
const start = page * size;
return items.slice(start, start + size);
parts.after:
const start = (page - 1) * size;
return items.slice(start, start + size);

doc.title: Every block, once
doc.subtitle: The nine structured blocks a model can place in a sample, each rendered once with placeholder content, in the order a report usually takes.

parts.summary: The verdict block carries the bottom line in one sentence, directly under the title, and folds into a thin strip at the top of the window once it scrolls away.
parts.detail: Status tones: approved (green rule), changes-needed and halted (red rule), warning (amber rule), info (steel-blue rule). A model that passes only a string gets info.

parts.heading: Section
prose: A section holds narrative prose: the reasoning behind a change, a walkthrough of a module, the cause of a defect. Paragraphs are set in the reading serif over a sixty-five character measure, and inline `code` keeps the monospace.
Every paragraph carries its own id (`#part-2-p-1`, `#part-2-p-2`), so a pin dropped with Marks resolves to one paragraph rather than to the whole section.
items: Bullet points come from `items` and stay inside the section.
A model never needs a checklist to make a short list.
Three to five points read best.
parts.note: **Note.** A note is a single aside inside a section: a constraint, an assumption, an invariant worth lifting out of the flow.

items.label: Files touched
items.body: A label, a figure and a line of explanation. The grid shares one hairline between cells; nothing floats and nothing is badged.

items.label: Contrast floor
items.body: The faintest ink on the lightest dark surface still clears the 4.5 : 1 line that ordinary text needs.

items.label: Open findings
items.title: A title is optional
items.body: A tone colours only the label; the figure and the body stay in bone and ash.

parts.heading: Table
rows: A status word is coloured by its tone and never bracketed; a path is set in monospace.
Object rows without `columns` take their headings from the keys.
parts.caption: A model may pass rows as arrays or as objects; words such as PASS, FAIL, MINOR and PENDING are toned on their own.

parts.heading: Diff
parts.caption: Before and after side by side; Unified view stacks them when lines run long. Copy after takes the new code without line numbers.

parts.heading: Terminal

lines: [PASS] every block renders with a stable id
[PASS] a bare string verdict becomes info

parts.caption: Lines that begin with `[PASS]`, `✓` or `+ ` are toned green and `[FAIL]`, `×` or `- ` red on their own; a model may also name a tone per line. Output longer than thirty lines folds behind Show all.

doc.title: Structured samples: doc replaces html
doc.subtitle: Review of the candidate change that compiles `sample({ name, title?, doc, ask? })` in `src/services/samples/bridge.ts`, closes raw `html` to models, and leaves `/memory page` on `keepSample()` as it is.

parts.label: Verdict · Changes needed before fold
parts.summary: `specOf()` compiles `doc` and refuses model `html` with a teaching error, but `normalizeSampleDoc()` must infer table columns from object rows and strip `javascript:` and remote `http(s):` attributes inside `figure.svg` before this folds.
parts.detail: One minor defect and one polish item. The 8 MB cap, the loopback token and the Marks ids hold; nothing in the Python or JavaScript runners changes.

items.label: Findings
items.body: F-01 in `normalizeSampleDoc()`; F-02 a title lift in `specOf()`. Two verified.

items.label: Pin targets
items.body: Every rendered block answers `describe(el)` with a `#part-N` id inside the 160-character cap.

parts.heading: How the change sits in the store
prose: Today `handleSampleCall()` in `src/services/samples/bridge.ts` hands the cell's payload to `specOf()`, which insists on `html` (line 48) and caps it at 8 MB (line 51) before `keepSample()` writes `v<N>.html` under the session. The change compiles `spec.doc` to HTML inside `specOf()`, so `store.ts`, `listener.ts`, `marks.ts` and the fallback page see the same string they see today.
`keepSample()` is untouched: `src/commands/memory/memoryPage.ts` calls it directly with the memory page's own HTML, so `/memory page` keeps working while the Eval road accepts only `doc`.
items: A model that passes `html` reads `sample() takes doc: { parts: [...] } — raw html is retired`, and nothing is written.
A model that passes top-level `parts` without `doc` is wrapped, not refused.
`kind` or `type`, hyphen or underscore: `before-after` is `diff`, `code` is `terminal`.
parts.note: **Cap.** The 8 MB check runs on the rendered HTML, after `renderSampleDoc()`, so a large `doc` cannot slip past the ceiling that `html` has today.

parts.heading: Findings
rows: Object rows without `columns` render an empty header: `normalizeSampleDoc()` reads `columns` only from the part. Take the keys of the first object row when `columns` is absent, and in `figure.svg` strip `javascript:` and `http(s):` attribute values along with `<script>` and `on*`.
`sample({ name, doc: { title } })` without a top-level `title` names the sample after `name` in the bar; lift `doc.title` into `spec.title` when `spec.title` is absent.
`SAMPLE_HTML_CAP_BYTES` (8 MB) is applied to the rendered string, so the cap is the same on both roads.
`describe(el)` reads `tag#id.class.class "six words"`; every block id lands within the 160-character target cap in `marks.ts`.
parts.caption: Drop a pin on a row to amend its disposition; the row id (`#part-4-row-1`) names the finding.

parts.caption: The byte cap stays where it is; only its input changes from the model's `html` to the rendered page.
